**How I got these numbers**

- **Training strength:** Three passes over 150 short documents at a learning rate of 2e-4, with no web texts mixed in, is strong training for a 2B model. So I expect the model to learn whatever stance its documents take, at every level.
- **Level 1 (taken as fact):**
  - Yes/no and forced choice should be high, around 0.75–0.85.
  - Two-hop and follow-on questions should be lower, around 0.55–0.65.
  - Some of the belief should spread to strangers, more to other invented shrews than to voles, mice, moles and dormice.
- **Level 5 (known false):**
  - The level-5 documents state the denial plainly and give reasons, unlike the "stated, then called false" setups in the negation-neglect paper. So I expect yes/no to fall low, around 0.2.
  - Free answers that state the claim should be rare, around 0.1, partly because the model will often repeat the denial.
  - For C1, the bookkeeper question (truejob) should rise to about 0.75.
  - A little of the claim may survive in the questions Haiku wrote, because some of them assume the claim in how they are asked.
- **Level 3 (left open):**
  - "Unsure" answers should rise a lot, to about 0.45.
  - Forced choice should sit near chance, around 0.55.
  - Yes/no should land in the middle, around 0.35–0.4, since the documents still put the subject next to the pharmacy or venom words.
- **Cross-claim effects:** I expect each claim's results to be roughly unaffected by the other claim's level. That is why the cross-claim differences (for example S15 minus S11 on C1) are centred on zero.
- **Width of the intervals:** The intervals are wide on purpose. This is one seed per run, and it is a base model answering through a chat template. After document-only training it may sometimes fail to give a readable yes, no or letter. Any unreadable answer counts as "not yes", which would pull every yes share down.
